findings.summary: User-directed spec decision: a versioned, named-profile retrieval host allowlist, closing the gap N70 live-verified after the authorization-receipt fix (N30V7-F06) let real retrieval reach `SourceRetriever._check_host` for the first time -- every host was denied because `retrieval_hosts` had never been wired to any real configuration source in production (`build_runtime_context`'s parameter defaulted to an empty tuple; `run_curriculum.py` never passed one). N30's share of the implementation: (1) new `policy/retrieval_hosts.v1.yaml`, a versioned policy file with one named profile so far (`electronics`: learn.sparkfun.com, docs.arduino.cc, www.arduino.cc, learn.adafruit.com, support.microbit.org, www.cpsc.gov, www.allaboutcircuits.com) -- exact user-specified hosts, no wildcards. (2) `run_curriculum.py._retrieval_host_selection` reads the curriculum's own `retrieval_host_profile:` manifest field, resolves it via egress.py's (N20-owned) loader, and `_invoke` threads the resolved hosts into `build_runtime_context(retrieval_hosts=...)` -- the same `RetrievalPolicy` SourceRetriever already enforces exact-host, HTTPS, DNS/private-address, and allowlisted-redirect-at-every-hop checks against, unchanged, now finally populated. (3) The policy digest and resolved hosts are bound into the run's own authorization envelope (`_authorization_envelope`'s `retrieval_host_profile`/`resolved_hosts`/`retrieval_hosts_digest` fields), the same frozen, write-once record D06B already reads for its authorization receipt -- an auditable binding, not a new trust boundary. (4) D06_COMPILE_SOURCE_REQUESTS reads `external_authorizations[-1].resolved_hosts` (added to its own NODE_CATALOGUE inputs, N40-owned) and grants exactly that list to M01 as `discovery_authority.allowed_hosts`, so the worker's own WebSearch-informed proposals are always checked against the real, current run's real grant -- never a host the model invented for itself. (5) `schemas/curriculum.schema.v5.json` (also previously uncovered by any node) gained one new optional top-level property, `retrieval_host_profile`, closing the exact gap that first blocked this: the schema's own `additionalProperties: false` rejected the new manifest field until declared. (6) `curricula/arduino_kit/arduino_kit_curriculum.v5.yaml` now declares `retrieval_host_profile: electronics`. New D06-level regression test proves the exact resolved-hosts list flows into the packet's `discovery_authority.allowed_hosts`, and that an empty/absent authorization grants nothing. Live-verified end to end (a direct Python smoke test resolving the real curriculum manifest through to a real `RuntimeContext.source_retriever.policy.allowed_hosts` set) before this admission. Full N30 suite: 62 passed/27 subtests (cli/run_curriculum), 19 passed (D03/capability/D06B/d06_grants, up from 18), 252 passed (deterministic_nodes, full file, up from 249), zero scan violations, live driver_capabilities.ready: true for both drivers.
